title: Atheism, Orthodoxy or Catholicism: which premises and which numbers does each conclusion actually depend on, once the arguments are machine-checked and the evidence is a likelihood-ratio ledger?
lede: research programme: 11 arguments for and against God and between Rome and Orthodoxy machine-checked with their cruxes computed (the modal ontological argument needs system B, its atheist mirror only T); in a sourced Bayes-factor ledger the resurrection testimony carries 98.5% of the variance on Christianity and needs a Bayes factor of only about 7 under even priors, while the prior outweighs every theism-vs-naturalism evidence item; Anderson's repair of Gödel's ontological proof avoids modal collapse exactly because it drops half of Scott's A2 (proved in Lean 4); with Anderson's intended varying domains the conclusion follows in every model but rests on the necessary-existence axiom (Lean 4, 17,440 frames checked), yet only de dicto: one God-like being existing at every world does not follow unless the properties separate individuals (Lean 4 countermodel), or unless "exists at every world" is itself made positive, a premise that closes the gap in every model and, past 6 cells, is independent of Anderson's rather than stronger (Lean 4, 8-cell countermodel)
summary: An open programme that puts the case between naturalism, Eastern Orthodox Christianity and Catholicism into two checkable forms. Logic: a stdlib decision procedure (S5 exact by Ladner’s bound; monadic first-order exact by a small-model argument) decides 11 arguments and computes their minimal inconsistent premise sets, with Lean 4 versions of each proof. All are valid as stated, so validity never settles anything. The Hartshorne–Plantinga modal ontological argument needs a symmetric accessibility relation (valid in B and S5, two-world countermodels in T and S4), while its reverse (“possibly no maximally great being exists”) is valid already in T. The Honorius and Florence disputes have exactly two minimal inconsistent sets and 16 coherent positions; Catholicism and Orthodoxy each drop two claims. Evidence: a 13-item likelihood-ratio ledger, each entry labelled published, argued or swept, reproduces Unwin’s 67% exactly. The resurrection testimony carries 98.5% of the variance of Christianity-vs-rest log odds; the Bayes factor it needs for P(Christian) > 0.5 is 7.3 under even priors (0.5 to 294 across a 3×3 prior grid), between a sceptic’s 1 and the McGrews’ 1044. For theism vs naturalism the prior carries 54% of the variance and swept fine-tuning 31%. Milestone 2: a leave-one-out shows the midpoint P(naturalism) of 0.76 rests on three items (dropping natural evil, moral evil or hiddenness each takes it to 0.5 or below), which the variance shares alone hide; and an exhaustive S5 model search finds Scott’s version of Gödel’s argument satisfiable only in one-world models (modal collapse). A proof (E10) then characterises every finite model of Anderson’s repair: a model exists exactly when the property algebra has a block made of whole individuals, so the God-like individual has no contingent property and no contingent proposition is expressible as a property; exhaustive search agrees on all 563 algebras checked. Correction (E11): that result uses Scott’s A2; Anderson keeps only “if a property is positive its complement is not”. With his own A2 the models are the principal filters at a hull H that is the union of exactly the rows whose hull is H, so under full property semantics every individual gives one model at every number of worlds and modal collapse is not forced; proved in Lean 4 and checked on 573 algebras. Varying domains (E12): with worlds of different domains and actualist quantifiers, every model of Anderson’s four axioms has a God-like individual existing at every world (Lean 4), but the axiom “necessary existence is positive” now carries the weight: without it 1,612 of 8,534 models have a world with no God-like existent; under full semantics a model exists exactly for each individual present at every world. Search and prediction agree on all 17,440 frames checked. Read with an actualist “has f necessarily” (E13) the same holds, but only de dicto: in 580 of 3,638 models (382 of 6,706 under the possibilist reading) God-likeness is shared by individuals that each exist at only some worlds, so “something God-like necessarily exists” does not follow unless the property space separates individuals (Lean 4 countermodel with two worlds, two individuals, one block). Replacing Anderson’s essence-based necessary existence by plain “exists at every world” as the positive property (E14) closes the gap: every God-like individual of every model then exists at every world (Lean 4, any algebra and domains); every such model also satisfies Anderson’s axiom in the 17,440 frames up to 6 cells (2,516 of the 3,638 models survive, all 580 de re failures among those lost), but not beyond (E15): an exact census finds 4,608 of 57,413 such models at 2 worlds × 4 individuals and 11,520 of 160,645 at 3 × 3 where Anderson’s axiom fails, with an 8-cell countermodel proved in Lean 4. Given A1 and plain necessary existence, Anderson’s axiom holds exactly when his necessary existents form a property of the algebra (Lean 4), so the two axioms are independent, not nested. Our finite semantics reproduces all 21 claims (17 theorems, 4 countermodels) of the published Isabelle/HOL formalisation of Fitting’s variant (Archive of Formal Proofs) across 2,070,148 frames in modal logics K and S5; without the rigid-positivity axiom the de re conclusion still holds in K, but the de dicto one fails (Lean 4). The same check on the AFP’s formalisation of Anderson’s variant reproduces every claim across 8,112,532 frames and shows the conclusion needs only a symmetric accessibility relation: it holds in every symmetric frame without reflexivity, transitivity or rigid positivity, and fails in S4 in 96,036 of 136,466 models (Lean 4, any frame and property collection). Its middle steps (God-likeness is an essence; a God-like being exists at every accessible world) hold in every Kripke frame once the properties can tell individuals apart, as under full semantics (Lean 4; 0 failures in 71,002 such models), while the conclusion still needs symmetry, with a Lean-certified S4 countermodel under full semantics. With rigid positivity, God-likeness is an essence at every world whose accessible worlds each lie on some cycle, and over 6,884,324 frames up to 3 worlds failures occur exactly at the other worlds (proved exact at every size in Lean 4). Without rigid positivity the exact condition is also proved, over general property collections: the step holds at w iff every world v that w sees has a world u reachable from v that sees v and sees only worlds w sees; E21’s 24 apparent exceptions were an artefact of searching only block algebras. Over block algebras, where every property has a complement, the exact condition is different and also proved: no successor v of w admits sets A ⊇ R(w) and S omitting v with, at every world t reachable from v, R(t) ⊆ A iff R(t) ⊆ S and R(t) missing A iff missing S (10,464 vs 14,688 failing pairs at 4 worlds). Limits: most ranges are swept, not sourced; the church-level ratios are symmetric placeholders until elicited. These are model outputs given stated inputs, not findings about whether God exists. Swinburne’s 0.97 for the incarnation and resurrection reproduces exactly (100/103) from his four inputs as quoted in Otte’s review; the historical evidence enters as a likelihood ratio of only 100, and the result falls below 1/2 if P(evidence | no incarnation) rises from 1/1000 to 1/30 (E25). The McGrews’ 1044, read in their own text, is exactly 102 (women) × 1039 (thirteen disciples at 103, multiplied as independent) × 103 (Paul); a mixture bound shows the disciples’ factor is at most 1/q, where q is the probability, given no resurrection, of one explanation covering the whole group, so their own 10−3 for a vision theory, read at group level, caps the case at 108: still far above the 7.3 the ledger needs at even priors, but short of overcoming their illustrative 10−40 prior (E26). E24’s separability condition has no closed form unless P = NP: a reduction from hypergraph 2-colouring, proved in Lean 4, makes deciding it NP-complete, so whether the essence step holds in every block-algebra model is coNP-complete for finite frames, while over general collections it is polynomial; checked on every serial relation up to 4 worlds and 2,046 hypergraphs, with a 16-world Fano-plane frame separating the two settings (E27). The hardness survives reflexivity but not transitivity or symmetry: a reflexive (KT) reduction, proved in Lean 4, keeps separability NP-complete in T, while in any frame where v can see back to w (so B and S5) no successor is separable and in a transitive frame v is separable iff it does not see itself, so without A4a the essence step holds at every world in S4, B and S5 and is coNP-complete to check in K, KD and T (E28). On Euclidean (axiom 5) frames the test is linear: a successor v is separable iff it sees a world w does not, never in S5, K45 or KD45, and it coincides with the condition over general property collections, so with E27 and E28 all fifteen logics of the modal cube are placed: coNP-complete in K, KD and KT, linear in K4, KD4, K5 and KD5, always holding in the rest (Lean 4; E29).
